newsitem.title: USA: First Union to acquire Keystone Investments.
newsitem.headline: First Union to acquire Keystone Investments.

text.p: First Union Corp said Friday it had agreed to acquire Keystone Investments Inc in exchange for 2,912,000 First Union shares.
First Union said Boston-based Keystone is an investment management and mutual fund company with $11.6 billion in assets under management.

This acquisition, combined with the Evergreen family of mutual funds managed by First Union, will create a mutual fund complex consisting of 69 individual mutual funds and nearly $27 billion in assets under management, it said.
First Union said the transaction will be accounted for as a pooling of interests.
It said the shares to be issued are valued at about $183 million based on its Thursday closing price of $62.875 a share.
First Union said it will also assume some $106 million of net debt from Keystone.

With the acquisition, First Union said, it will become the third-largest bank-advised mutual fund organization in the U.S., the second-largest bank manager of equity mutual fund assets, and the 27th-largest mutual fund manager, based on mutual fund assets under management.
The transaction will provide national and global distribution capabilities, a broadened mutual fund product line, and state-of-the art technology, First Union said.

The acquisition is expected to be accretive to earnings per share in 1998 and is scheduled to close in late 1996 or early 1997, subject to approval by shareholders of the Keystone family of mutual funds, regulatory approval, and other conditions, First Union said.
